column8: Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Adams set the pencil aside because pencil was presumed deliberative, so a judge hears ink as decided and pencil as undecided, and would read the planned 2031 move as undecided (guard 3, IPS l.15; the card's own row 36). The deletion test stands on NUMBERS 4 and V2.2's 3e turn without the court, and 3e's prose carries no payout figure, so never $103,178 there (coherence reader 7, M6). Stays in the store as the recorded disanalogy.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Counsel's line reads ink as a final intention and pencil as a deliberative one, the decided sense; it is argument, not the holding, and always overstates (rows 7-10). The labels beside model figures are Book 10's rule already. Store as disanalogy.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Final and absolute against deliberative is the decided reading in its plainest form, and durability-to-finality maps ink to a final act, not to ownership. Its theme is Q47 A14 (iron gall against carbon), which V2.2 2.2 already holds as the optional turn. The 1828 reports were not read.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. A pencil signature pushes straight to the signed reading (the card's claim 3, row 37). The contrast it offers (a presumption is inferred, ownership is checked) needs no case. Store as disanalogy.

Tue 17 Nov: a guard for the writers, never report prose. The law accepts pencil as writing (Geary 1826; Wills Act 1837), so never say the law treats pencil as provisional. A signing case, so it is never a turn.
Tue 17 Nov: the same guard as row 5, read only in Mason's summary (Jollie v Lennie not opened); carry it there as the modern example if the guard is ever needed.

Tue 17 Nov: a guard with rows 8-10: the pencil presumption is England's and rebuttable, and American courts rejected it, so there is no single legal view to borrow. Store only; wills are the decided sense. Tomlinson itself not opened.
Tue 17 Nov: West Virginia's rejection, read at source; carry it under row 7's guard as the plainest American quote.
Tue 17 Nov: the US split (New Hampshire and Indiana), read at source; it belongs under row 7's guard that the presumption is a rebuttable guess, and only in some places.
Tue 17 Nov: England's own judges made intent decide, not the medium; carry under row 7. Dickinson itself not read.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. A pencil mark read as a final decision makes the medium stand for decided, the reading tonight's rule keeps out. The labelling job it proposes (we modelled, on today's figures) is Book 10's rule already and needs no 1945 court.

Tue 17 Nov: store only. Pencil can be effaced is the conceit's own premise (Martin 2019, p. 6); 3c's reason for stating nothing before the move is NUMBERS 4's 10.7%, worded as the row words it (a top stated a year early, about 11 of 100 futures), and the drying-ink turn is retired, so a will case adds a source, not a job. Quote only the 1872 line, never the 1877 adjective.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. A pencil signature on a lease is the signed sense (the card's own critique), and its proposed home sits beside Laura's words to co-sponsors in 3d, where no comics word goes (guard 4). Store as disanalogy; the court text was read through a search index, not the page.

Tue 17 Nov: the rule-and-reading job is Q79-013's (keep, the geologic boundary and its date). Tipper is unverified (Mason's summary only) and is a guarantee, the signing sense, whose pencil reads as undecided.
Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Practitioners restate the deliberative presumption (pencil as undecided), the cases behind it unread, and Australia is not in the case, so it serves no part.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.0, the phrase only, said plainly: an inked figure will be paid with nothing more to happen (no deposit, no purchase, no market move), which is why the bottom waits for January 2028 and the top for the move. Never the will case, an intent test that reads ink as decided, and never Australian law; test the gloss cold with the definition first.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Webster moves from signed to intended, which is the decided reading, not to owned, so it is not the conceit's move; and naming signing beside the 2.0 definition invites the misreading card Q42 found. Store as disanalogy.

Tue 17 Nov: writers' evidence, never report prose: ISO 11798's own scope sets lasting apart from authenticity, which backs V2.1's owned against the signed reading (card Q42). Naming signing in the report would invite the very misreading.

Tue 17 Nov: store only. Time tests the pencil and terms make the ink is true, but its job is done by aha 7 (the forecast barely touches the promise) and the deletion test (NUMBERS 4); the carbon-ink fact is Q47 A14's. Hard to say in one sentence.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, a craft fact behind V2.2's a US default is the paper: documentary ink is defined by a line that survives until the paper itself is damaged. One plain clause at most, the standard in References only, never as an image of its own; use the test, never documentary use or evidence (the signing sense). 1998 edition read; test methods unread.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c, the strongest fact behind the conceit on the card: in the US National Archives only pencil may be used beside an original record (36 CFR 1254.36(a)). It can carry non-photo blue's job (models shown to judges, owned figures untouched) with no trade word, which panel 3 asked for; one turn per part, so it replaces non-photo blue, never sits beside it. It maps only the models, since VT, the deposit and her income are pencil too and are not readers' notes. Cold test with the definition first.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.5, the fact only (an accidental ink mark is permanent) backs the click's plain reason, there's no rubbing it out, already in the same sentence (round 6). Drop the mapping to the one-owner rule: an archive rule beside the click stacks a second image (round 2: stacked turns heard as the team's 0 of 24). Store only.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: support for the guard never ink is permanent and for Q47 row 17 (a dated Treasury against a bond fund with no end date); archival pens would be a second image, which tonight's voice round says fails.

Tue 17 Nov: the UK twin of row 21; if row 21 is used, its plainest line (bring a pencil, ink is not allowed near the records) may be the quote. Never nothing can change (a missed deposit or a default can); the no-eraser mapping to a market fall is already 3e's two reasons (IPS l.17).

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Ruling a blank shut before an entry is certified is the signed sense, and the card's own critique kills the closed-page mapping (Laura may still give from her flexibility, CONCEIT 5b rank 1). Read only in a reproduction.
Tue 17 Nov: writers' evidence, never report prose: the law's own phrase for ink (a wet signature) is a signature, which is why V2.1 defines ink with owned (card Q42).
Tue 17 Nov: the same evidence as row 26 (ink as signing); its readable struck-through correction is card Q106's (rows 10-11).

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. A pleading in ink is a party's own assertion, so the higher-bar mapping makes ink a signed or asserted statement, not owned money; its home is 3d beside Laura's words to co-sponsors (guard 4); and the case leaves Taiwan's law out.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. The ruling is about signing official papers (the card's own claim 3), and calling a top stated early ink that heat can erase gives the word ink to a figure she does not own, bending V2.1's definition (round 6's warning on the click); a friction pen is a second image needing setup, which tonight's voice round says fails. Its 11-in-100 wording is right and stays in NUMBERS 4. Store as disanalogy.
Tue 17 Nov: a guard only: never say Taiwan's document manual requires ink for official papers (it does not say).
Tue 17 Nov: store only: court ink rules serve legibility and are the signing sense (row 37); no part needs them.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.2, Bigelow's line alone (any material permanent enough to hold its language) may back V2.2's permanence is judged on the payment date (IPS l.13). Drop Geary: a pencil indorsement is the signing sense and makes pencil good enough for a short promise, which inverts the conceit. 3a's extra Treasuries need no will law; Bigelow's edition year unverified.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse. Here the dropped layer is the ink (the form's template), which reverses V2.1's ink as owned; it is a second image beside non-photo blue, the card itself prefers non-photo blue, and one sentence of the source was cut off.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse for the report. Cheque ink is the signing sense (row 37; rater AT refused Q106-031 for the same reason), and the guard it backs (never ink is permanent; ink holds because each Treasury is held to its date) is already CONCEIT section 2 and Q47 A13.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse. A probate form makes the inked blanks the testator's decision (the decided sense), and the printed form is a third term beside pencil and ink (card Q42). Round 6's two inkings, two dates works as a plain verb and needs no precedent.

Tue 17 Nov: the writers' guard for 2.0 and 3c is right: the law's pencil means undecided, the plan's not yet owned, and the 2028 order and the move are fixed in IPS l.13, l.15 and l.17. Drop its allowance: under tonight's rule no probate case is used in the report, not even a court read only the ink (row 1).

Tue 17 Nov: the list of signing parallels is right; add rows 1-3, 11, 15-17, 28 and 35 (probate and court ink read as decided or signed) and drop the two exceptions, since Kleine (3d) and the friction pen (3c) push the signed sense too.

Tue 17 Nov: cut the shortlist for the 27 Nov writers to the archive rule (row 21, 3c, cold test first), ISO 12757-2's paper-before-line test (row 20, a fact behind 3e) and ISO 11798's scope (row 18, writers' evidence only). Adams, without more and Webster are intent tests that read ink as decided.

Tue 17 Nov: the synthesis of row 21 (ink reserved to the record, every model a reader's pencil); carry its disanalogy there: the archive's reason is physical damage, Laura's is credibility (the case).
